posts.t:
gigiocean wrote: Hi bulbuli..my problem is how to identify stacked zones on my chart.

Gigiocean,

I think bulbuli is right. Actually, you are referring to Stacked Supply/Demand Zones.

The screenshot below from this post, shows stacked Supply Zones. How do you find them? The same way that you find all supply and demand zones. Higher highs or lower lows will tell you the zones. We call HHs and LLs FTRs. Each FTR is a new level of supply or demand. You can see there are many ways to say the same thing. Even further, If is quoted as saying that an FTR is a Flag Limit (hereand here ).

This screenshot from this article, shows the PAZs lined up in between the Supply and Demand Zones. The green zones are supply and demand zones that are stacked on top of one another. The PAZs are also stacked. It would appear that in order for stacked zones to exist there must be a trend.

Does this clear things up at all?
posts.fa:
gigiocean نوشت: سلام bulbuli… مشکل من این است که چطور نواحی انباشته‌شده را روی چارت تشخیص بدهم.

Gigiocean،

فکر می‌کنم bulbuli درست می‌گوید. در واقع، تو به نواحی انباشته‌شدهٔ عرضه/تقاضا اشاره می‌کنی.

عکس از صفحه پایین از این پست، نواحی عرضهٔ انباشته‌شده را نشان می‌دهد. چطور پیدایشان می‌کنی؟ همان‌طور که همهٔ نواحی عرضه و تقاضا را پیدا می‌کنی. سقف‌های بالاتر یا کف‌های پایین‌تر نواحی را به تو می‌گویند. ما HH‌ها و LL‌ها را FTR می‌نامیم. هر FTR یک سطح جدید عرضه یا تقاضا است. می‌بینی راه‌های زیادی برای گفتن یک چیز هست. حتی بیشتر، IF نقل‌قول شده که می‌گوید یک FTR یک FL است (اینجا و اینجا ).

این عکس از صفحه از این مقاله، PAZ‌ها را نشان می‌دهد که بین نواحی عرضه و تقاضا چیده شده‌اند. نواحی سبز عرضه و تقاضا هستند که روی هم انباشته شده‌اند. PAZ‌ها هم انباشته‌اند. به نظر می‌رسد برای وجود نواحی انباشته‌شده باید یک روند باشد.

آیا این چیزها را روشن کرد؟

posts.t:
Hi Gigiocean,

I have marked below an example of stacked supply zones. Here, by 'stacked zones' we mean that the Decision Points (Be it Supply or demand or FTRs) are arranged very closed to one another and so prices may ignore the intermediate levels to reach the next or outermost level (the highest supply zone here in example).

And so there is no difference between both PAZs, it is just a matter of how they are seen in the chart. Hope it helps

Just thought I would post something I'm watching so others can comment.

The big picture is on the left panel. Price engulfs an important swing low from a recent series of lows at

and creates a flag limit

. We zoom in on the middle panel to get a

better picture of what's going on, and notice there may be an even better R/R opportunity. We see that when the low of our flag limit (

), which is itself a flag, was

broken, we had an FTR or new flag limit created when price tried to get back into our zone at

. Now that we have a place to watch for an entry, depending on how price

moves back up to it, we need to consider a target. In the far right panel we see that we had an FTR which was holding up price. It has since been tapped a first time and now a second after price just recently dropped. To me this indicates the area is likely consumed. A good target might be a little above where I've marked the red horizontal rule at D, which is actually the FTR for a wider area if my analysis is correct. Risk:Reward is about 1:7.
